finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The code does not involve any user input or external data that could be manipulated to inject commands. The signal handling is controlled and does not involve any command execution.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The sink `kill(getppid(), SIGINT)` is not an OS command execution point; it merely sends a signal to the parent process. The signal value is a compile‑time constant (`SIGINT`), and there is no user‑supplied or environment‑derived value involved. Therefore there is no path from an untrusted source to a command execution facility, and the reported OS Command Injection claim is incorrect.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.trigger: Reading and writing to the pipe with a single byte buffer
finding.assumptions: The pipe communication is used for synchronization and does not involve any user input or external data that could be manipulated to inject commands.

parsed.refutation_attempt:
1) Verified that the only data passed through the pipe is the hardcoded character 'r' written at line 62 and read at line 52. No external input (stdin, file, network, argv, environment, IPC from untrusted source) can influence this value.
2) The read() and write() calls are used solely for inter‑process synchronization; they do not form part of an OS command string or invoke a shell.
3) There is no subsequent use of the pipe data in a system(), exec*, or similar call that would execute an external command.
Thus the conditions for OS Command Injection (CWE‑77) are not satisfied.

finding.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
finding.trigger: Reading and writing to the pipe with a single byte buffer
finding.assumptions: The pipe communication is used for synchronization and does not involve any user input or external data that could cause integer overflow.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the size argument passed to read() and write() is a constant literal (1) on lines 52 and 62; since the value is hard‑coded and small, no integer overflow or wraparound can occur. The data read/written is from a pipe used solely for synchronization, not from any untrusted source.

finding.title: Improper Release of a Resource ('Resource Leak')
finding.trigger: Setting the signal handler with SA_RESETHAND flag
finding.assumptions: The signal handler is reset to default after the first delivery, but there is no explicit check or cleanup for the pipe resources.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the pipe file descriptors are closed in both parent (line 59) and child (line 49) processes. The pipe is created once (line 18) and used for synchronization, with no remaining open descriptors after the child exits or the parent finishes. No resource is leaked. The SA_RESETHAND flag only affects signal handling semantics and does not introduce a resource leak. Thus the claim of a resource leak is unfounded.
